name: Truck / Twister
description: The truck position and Twister submission: from back or Side Control, lock a Body Triangle around the opponent's torso and pull their head toward their own hip to create a spinal lock.
shortInstruction: Body Triangle around the torso, pull the head to the hip, arch the back, the Twister is a spinal lock, not a choke.
summary: The truck is a specialized position where you control the opponent from the side with a Body Triangle (similar to the truck position in wrestling). From the truck, you can attack the Twister, a spinal lock that twists the opponent's spine by pulling their head toward their own hip. The Twister is not a choke or joint lock, it is a spinal lock that creates intense pressure on the vertebrae. It is no-gi specific (the gi makes it harder to maintain the Body Triangle) and is known for being extremely effective but requiring precise positioning.
whyItWorks: The Body Triangle prevents them from rolling or turning out of the position.
The spinal lock mechanism is unfamiliar to most opponents, they often do not know how to defend or escape.
The Twister can be chained into other submissions (Back Take, Armbar) when they defend.
Eddie Bravo / 10th Planet principle: the truck/Twister is the backbone of the 'Train of Pain', a complete attack chain.
commonMistakes: Not securing the Body Triangle before going for the Twister, the Body Triangle is the control position.
Pulling the head too aggressively, the Twister is a gradual twist, not a sudden jerk.
Letting their legs free from the Body Triangle, leg control is essential.
Attempting the Twister without controlling their far arm, they will post and prevent the rotation.
coachingCues: Head to the hip, arch the back, twist slowly.
Control the far arm, own the rotation.
The Twister is a gradual twist, not a jerk.
safetySummary: The Twister applies rotational pressure to the spine, this is one of the most dangerous submissions in BJJ.
Apply the Twister VERY slowly and release on ANY sign of discomfort.
Do not attempt the Twister on partners with pre-existing back or neck issues.
Tap early on spinal locks, spinal injuries can be permanent.
Not appropriate for beginners, requires advanced body awareness.
keyCorrections: If you can't feel the rotation, your Body Triangle is too loose, squeeze tighter.
If they defend the Twister by gripping their own leg, switch to the Armbar or Back Take.
If they roll through, follow their rotation and re-attack from the other side.

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Side Control or Half Guard: secure Body Triangle (truck position) → control far arm → pull their head toward their hip → arch your back → finish.

decisionTree.action: The truck/Twister chains with: Back Take (if they roll), Armbar (if they defend), or standard submission.
10th Planet system: the truck is the position; the Twister is one of many attacks from it.

moneyDetails: The Body Triangle should be around their torso at the waist level, not at their legs.
Your legs lock in a figure-four (Body Triangle), squeeze to compress their ribs and limit movement.
Control their far arm by pushing their elbow toward their head, this prevents them from posting.
The Twister finish: pull their head toward their own hip while arching your back, the rotation twists their spine.
nextStep: After the truck/Twister, learn the Back Take from the truck and the Calf Slicer from the same position.
fixItFast: Body Triangle too loose? Squeeze tighter and lock the figure-four deeper.
Can't twist? Control their far arm first, a free arm blocks the rotation.
They roll out? Follow their roll and take the back.
